R0209.title: Unauthorized Outbound Connection and C2 Control
R0209.definition: IoT devices infected with trojans actively connect to C2 servers to receive remote commands, becoming part of botnets.
keywords: Unauthorized Outbound Connection and C2 Control

references.title: Securing the Internet of Things (IoT) - CISA

R0209.description:
Unauthorized outbound connection and C2 control are typical signs of compromised devices. Infected devices connect to attacker infrastructure and receive commands for scanning, proxying, DDoS, data theft, or lateral movement.

IoT devices often sit at the network edge with limited logging and operations support, making them durable footholds. Enterprises need outbound baselines, domain and IP reputation checks, and device isolation.

Limitation: Requires breaching network isolation
R0209.influence: C2-controlled IoT devices can become botnet nodes, proxies, or internal footholds for data theft and lateral movement.

observables: IoT devices initiate persistent outbound connections to unfamiliar IPs or domains with no business justification
Device traffic shows C2 communication features such as fixed heartbeat intervals or encrypted beacons
Device behavior shifts from passive service to active outbound communication and command reception
Multiple devices on the same subnet reach out to the same external address around the same time
Device DNS queries hit known C2 or DGA domain signatures
